mines.mine_notes: One of four KGHM Polska Miedź underground copper-silver mines (Lubin, Rudna, Polkowice-Sieroszowice, Głogów Głęboki-Przemysłowy). Report does not split production or grades per mine; KGHM Polska Miedź S.A. segment FY2025: copper in concentrate 401.1 kt; silver in concentrate 1,321 t; electrolytic copper 570.9 kt (375.4 kt from own concentrate); metallic silver 1,323 t; total unit cost of electrolytic copper from own concentrate PLN28,786/t; C1 payable copper $3.16/lb (incl. mining taxes); C1 payable copper in concentrate $3.16/lb. Ore is enriched at the Ore Enrichment Plants; concentrates processed at Głogów I/II, Legnica, Cedynia smelters.

mines.mine_notes: Open-pit porphyry/skarn copper mine, White Pine County, Nevada. 2025: payable copper 49.3 kt; TPM 40.6 koz. LoM 11 years. End products: copper-gold concentrate and molybdenum concentrate. International segment C1 $1.03/lb (incl. taxes).
Open-pit oxide copper mine, Arizona; heap leach/SX-EW producing copper cathodes. 2025 payable copper 2.7 kt. LoM 4 years (Cactus pit Phase 3 extends to 2029).

Sold to Magna Mining Inc. via Project Nikolas Company Inc.; transaction finalised 28 February 2025 (McCreedy West producing, Levack/Morrison and Podolsky on care & maintenance, 5 exploration concessions). 2025 production (Jan–Feb only): payable copper 0.3 kt, TPM 2.8 koz. No longer held.

notes: Group FY2025: payable copper 710.0 kt (−2.7% y/y); payable silver 1,347 t (of which Poland 1,323 t metallic; Sierra Gorda/others ~24 t); group C1 payable copper cost $2.58/lb (incl. mining taxes; KGHM Polska $3.16, International $1.03, Sierra Gorda $0.86). Attributable silver ≈ 43.3 Moz (1,347 t × 32,150.7 oz/t). Revenue PLN36.4bn (+3%), adjusted EBITDA PLN10,276M (+22%), net profit PLN3,688M (+28%). USD conversion: average 2025 USD/PLN ≈ 3.66. Mine-level AISC, grades and per-mine reserves are not disclosed in the FY2025 Management Board report or financial statements; KGHM reports per-mine reserves only in dedicated mineral asset disclosures (not this report).
